limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by an agent that did not write or source-review the guide; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.
API sessions created prerequisites, played second actors' writes and read back saved state and refusals. Every guide step ran in the browser as the named role.

Other agents on this host create and remove lab networks. Chromium then aborted in-flight requests with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED and the app showed Something went wrong.; the scripts reload up to twice and log each retry under retries in the logs. 36 direct reloads of the affected Signatures pages afterwards showed no error page, so this is recorded as environment noise, not a product bug.

Run on the shared work lab (openlaw-docs-9d2b1705-work) with a Business User created by Portal sign-in (doc032.c2.bu@helix.example). MCP switches, Read-only and the Toolset ceiling were changed for single checks and put back at once (settingsChanged in walkthrough-troubleshooting.json).

No Toolsets are available for your account. was produced by setting the Toolset ceiling to Administration only: the Legal Team Member and the Business User saw the sentence and no Request a key; the Administrator still had Request a key.

The signing states ran on the owned lab openlaw-docs-9d2b1705-c2sign with the e2e signing stand-in and injected faults: envelope creation answered 500 (Creation uncertain), the executed download answered 503 until the fetch retries ran out (Filing the signed copy…, then The signed copy could not be filed. Upload it to the record instead.), and recovery_stopped was set in the lab database (Automatic recovery has stopped), because the 32-attempt limit cannot be reached in a walkthrough. Confirms the author's limitation: this is stand-in evidence, not live-provider evidence (#1178). The lab was destroyed after the run.
Filing the signed copy… was seen on the round whose download was failing; on the successful rounds the copy was filed before the first reload, so the interim text was not caught there.

Confirms the author's limitation that the partially signed path is built behavior: a No round filed a Partially signed copy, marked no Version executed and left the Contract at Partially signed (Signature Stage).
Analysis and AI conversion ran with AI disabled on the seed (as in DOC-030): the checks cover the settings, Fields header and manual conversion fallback, not a live provider run.
